newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-DONALD AND POLLOCK RETURN TO TEST INDIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DONALD AND POLLOCK RETURN TO TEST INDIA.

text.p: South African fast bowlers Allan Donald and Shaun Pollock return after injury to confront India on a pitch likely to provide both pace and bounce in the first test starting at Kingsmead on Thursday.

India face the opening game of the three-test rubber in confident mood after their recent 2-1 home series victory against South Africa, but can expect a stern examination from a threatening pace quartet of Donald and Pollock with all-rounders Brian McMillan and Lance Klusener.

Donald returns after suffering an ankle injury during the tour of India and Pollock makes his comeback following an operation on his left ankle which curtailed his first season in English county cricket with Warwickshire.

While India have Javagal Srinath and the rapidly emerging Venkatesh Prasad to take the new ball, captain Sachin Tendulkar's side do not possess sufficient back-up to take full advantage of the expected conditions.

The third seamer's slot in their test side is likely to be filled by single test cap David Johnson, who was not overly impressive on the slow Port Elizabeth pitch in their drawn tour opener against Eastern Province.
On the batting front, both sides are strong. While the gifted Tendulkar is overdue a return to his customary test form, Mohammad Azharuddin was in sublime touch against South Africa in India.

There may be a question mark about Azharuddin's ability to make test hundreds away from home on pitches containing a bit of pace and bounce, but he and Tendulkar form the quality backbone of India's batting. Much is also expected of the young talent of Saurav Ganguly and Rahul Dravid.
India's main batting weakness lies in their expected opening pair of Woorkeri Raman and Vikram Rathore, neither of whom appears to be reliable at test level.
But although Indian coach Madan Lal would have preferred one more tour match in South Africa before going into the first test, he remains confident about his side's batting.

"Although I would have liked my batsmen to have batted a little bit more, all of our top six got some time in the middle in Port Elizabeth. And most of them batted against South Africa in India, so they are pretty confident."
While South Africa's batting looked a little vulnerable on the under-prepared and slow pitches of India, it should be a very different matter during the home series.

Consistent opener Gary Kirsten and the elegant Daryll Cullinan have been the most reliable cogs in their batting line-up and captain Hansie Cronje, not at his best in recent tests, will feel a lot more comfortable on surfaces with more bounce.
The selection of young blood in the shape of in-form Adam Bacher, Herschelle Gibbs and Jacques Kallis also gives South Africa's batting a more competitive edge.

South Africa - Gary Kirsten, Andrew Hudson, Adam Bacher, Herschelle Gibbs, Daryll Cullinan, Hansie Cronje (captain), Jacques Kallis, Brian McMillan, Shaun Pollock, Lance Klusener, Dave Richardson, Allan Donald, Paul Adams.

India - Vikram Rathore, Woorkeri Raman, Saurav Ganguly, Sachin Tendulkar (captain), Mohammad Azharuddin, Rahul Dravid, V.V.S.Laxman, Nayan Mongia, David Johnson, Anil Kumble, Javagal Srinath, Venkatesh Prasad, Venkatapathy Raju.
